provenance: Recovered 2026-07-02 from the retired Base44 app (the-netify-sd-wan-sase-marketplace, public/rfp-question-bank/sase-v1.json, last_reviewed 2026-05-18). This is the full 43-question SASE canonical bank with evidence, sector-applicability, weighting, red-flag and follow-up metadata; the 27-question set previously in data/rfp-question-bank.json was a condensed port of this file.

questions.question: Describe how your platform enforces zero trust access to private applications.
questions.why_it_matters: Private application access is a core SASE use case and should be controlled by identity, device and application context rather than broad network access.
follow_up_questions: Can policies differ by user group and device posture?
Can access be restricted to specific private applications rather than subnets?

questions.question: Which identity providers do you support natively, and which protocols (SAML, OIDC, SCIM)?
questions.why_it_matters: Native IdP integration determines whether identity, group and lifecycle data drive access decisions in real time.
follow_up_questions: How are deprovisioning events handled end to end?

questions.question: How is device posture evaluated and used in access decisions?
questions.why_it_matters: Device posture lets buyers enforce different access rules for managed, unmanaged and high-risk devices.
red_flag_answers: Posture only on a single OS
follow_up_questions: Which posture signals are available on unmanaged devices?

questions.question: Describe step-up authentication and continuous session validation.
questions.why_it_matters: Continuous validation reduces the risk of stale sessions being used after the risk context changes.
follow_up_questions: Which signals can trigger step-up?

questions.question: Describe how third-party and contractor access is managed.
questions.why_it_matters: Third-party access is a common breach vector and needs tight, audited control.
follow_up_questions: Is access time-bound by default?

questions.question: Describe your secure web gateway, including TLS inspection and URL category coverage.
questions.why_it_matters: The SWG is the primary control plane for web traffic and must inspect TLS to be effective.
follow_up_questions: How are TLS exceptions managed for sensitive sites?

questions.question: Describe browser-based isolation options and use cases.
questions.why_it_matters: Isolation is a useful control for risky categories without blocking access.
follow_up_questions: Is isolation included or licensed separately?

questions.question: Describe your inline and API-based CASB coverage for sanctioned and shadow SaaS.
questions.why_it_matters: CASB visibility is needed to control data movement to SaaS and to detect shadow SaaS use.
red_flag_answers: Coverage of fewer than 10 major SaaS
follow_up_questions: How are shadow SaaS apps discovered and triaged?

questions.question: Describe your DLP capabilities, policy templates and incident workflow.
questions.why_it_matters: DLP is the primary control for preventing accidental and malicious data egress and must be content-aware.
follow_up_questions: Can DLP policies apply to unmanaged devices?

questions.question: How is policy kept consistent across managed and unmanaged devices?
questions.why_it_matters: Unmanaged devices are a common data egress channel and need consistent controls.
follow_up_questions: Which browsers and OSes are supported on unmanaged devices?

questions.question: Describe your cloud-delivered firewall, including layer-7 application controls.
questions.why_it_matters: FWaaS replaces branch firewalls and must provide consistent layer-7 controls.
follow_up_questions: How are policy changes audited?

questions.question: Describe your IPS, anti-malware and sandboxing stack and update frequency.
questions.why_it_matters: Threat protection effectiveness depends on inline inspection and timely intelligence.
red_flag_answers: Sandbox limited to a few file types
follow_up_questions: How are false positives triaged?

questions.question: How is policy kept consistent across branch, roaming and cloud egress traffic?
questions.why_it_matters: Inconsistent policy planes create gaps and operational overhead.
red_flag_answers: Separate policy engines per traffic type
follow_up_questions: How are policy conflicts resolved?

questions.question: Describe DNS-layer security and its integration with the rest of the stack.
questions.why_it_matters: DNS-layer controls catch threats early and protect off-network devices.
follow_up_questions: Does DNS security work off-network?

questions.question: Describe how SD-WAN integrates with your SSE stack.
questions.why_it_matters: Tight SD-WAN and SSE integration determines branch user experience and policy consistency.
red_flag_answers: Integration via IPsec only with no telemetry sharing
follow_up_questions: Is the SD-WAN supplied by you or a partner?

questions.question: How are SASE PoPs selected for each branch and how is performance measured?
questions.why_it_matters: PoP selection drives branch latency and user experience.
red_flag_answers: Static PoP assignment with no telemetry
follow_up_questions: How are PoP failovers handled?

questions.question: Describe link failover behaviour, including 4G/5G or LTE failover.
questions.why_it_matters: Failover behaviour determines store, plant and clinic uptime during link events.
follow_up_questions: Are critical applications kept on cellular failover?

questions.question: Describe direct internet breakout behaviour at branches.
questions.why_it_matters: Local breakout reduces backhaul cost but must keep security policy consistent.
follow_up_questions: Which SaaS apps are typically broken out locally?

questions.question: Describe segmentation options for OT or sensitive networks at branch and plant sites.
questions.why_it_matters: Segmentation between OT and IT is essential in industrial environments.
follow_up_questions: Which industrial protocols are supported?

questions.question: Which log types are captured and what retention options are available?
questions.why_it_matters: Log coverage and retention drive audit, investigation and regulatory reporting.
red_flag_answers: Short fixed retention with no export
follow_up_questions: Are logs tamper-evident?

questions.question: How can logs be exported to our SIEM or storage?
questions.why_it_matters: Buyers need logs in their own SIEM for correlation and long-term retention.
follow_up_questions: Is export available in near real time?

questions.question: How are administrative actions audited?
questions.why_it_matters: Admin audit trails are required for regulatory and forensic purposes.
follow_up_questions: Can admin logs be exported to a separate audit store?

questions.question: How are user-experience metrics collected and shared?
questions.why_it_matters: UX telemetry helps prove SASE delivers a better user experience.
follow_up_questions: Are UX metrics available per site and per user?

questions.question: Where are customer data, logs and metadata stored and processed?
questions.why_it_matters: Data residency drives regulatory compliance and contractual obligations.
follow_up_questions: Can residency be enforced for logs separately from tenant config?

questions.question: List your sub-processors and their locations.
questions.why_it_matters: Sub-processor disclosure is required for many regulated buyers.
follow_up_questions: How are sub-processor changes notified?

questions.question: Describe support access controls and the regions from which support operates.
questions.why_it_matters: Support access can introduce cross-border data exposure if not controlled.
follow_up_questions: Can support access be restricted to named regions?

questions.question: Describe support for customer-managed encryption keys.
questions.why_it_matters: CMK can be a requirement for highly regulated workloads.
follow_up_questions: Which modules support CMK?

questions.question: Describe your service model, including managed, co-managed and self-managed options.
questions.why_it_matters: The service model defines the split of responsibilities and informs operational cost.
follow_up_questions: Can the split change over the term?

questions.question: What SLAs apply to support response, restoration and change requests?
questions.why_it_matters: Operational SLAs matter more than platform availability for day-to-day experience.
follow_up_questions: How are SLA credits calculated and applied?

questions.question: How are service reviews structured and how often do they occur?
questions.why_it_matters: Regular reviews keep the service aligned with buyer priorities.
follow_up_questions: Who attends reviews on your side?

questions.question: Describe escalation paths, including out-of-hours.
questions.why_it_matters: Escalation matters most when incidents occur outside business hours.
follow_up_questions: Is out-of-hours included or chargeable?

questions.question: Describe a typical deployment plan for an estate of our size.
questions.why_it_matters: A credible deployment plan reduces project risk and surprises.
follow_up_questions: What are typical milestone durations?

questions.question: How is configuration automated for sites, users and policy?
questions.why_it_matters: Automation drives rollout speed and consistency across multi-site estates.
follow_up_questions: Is configuration declarative or imperative?

questions.question: How are changes tested and rolled back?
questions.why_it_matters: Tested change and rollback procedures reduce outage risk.
follow_up_questions: Can changes be applied to a staged set first?

questions.question: How are user agents and clients distributed and updated?
questions.why_it_matters: Agent updates impact user experience and security posture.
follow_up_questions: Are updates staged and reversible?

questions.question: Describe your pricing model and what is included.
questions.why_it_matters: Clarity on the pricing model drives like-for-like supplier comparison.
follow_up_questions: Which modules are licensed separately?

questions.question: Provide a worked example for our user and site count.
questions.why_it_matters: Worked examples expose hidden charges and reveal true unit cost.
follow_up_questions: What is the cost of doubling the user count?

questions.question: How are growth and reductions handled within the term?
questions.why_it_matters: Flex terms determine commercial exposure if estate size changes.
red_flag_answers: No reduction allowed during the term
follow_up_questions: Is there a flex range that does not require renegotiation?

questions.question: List all items priced separately, including professional services.
questions.why_it_matters: Add-ons drive total cost of ownership and must be transparent.
follow_up_questions: Which add-ons are commonly required for our use case?

questions.question: Provide your current certifications and expiry dates.
questions.why_it_matters: Current certifications support regulated buyer due diligence.
follow_up_questions: Which auditor performed the most recent audit?

questions.question: Share recent independent test results relevant to SASE.
questions.why_it_matters: Independent test results reduce reliance on vendor claims.
follow_up_questions: When were the tests conducted?

questions.question: Provide customer references in our sector.
questions.why_it_matters: Sector-specific references increase confidence in fit.
follow_up_questions: Can a reference call be arranged?

questions.question: Provide details of any recent security incidents and your handling of them.
questions.why_it_matters: Incident handling history shows operational maturity.
follow_up_questions: What changed after the most recent incident?
